newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese yuan ends down at intra-day low vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Chinese yuan ends down at intra-day low vs dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan ended down at an intra-day low of 8.2983 against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday on the Shanghai-based China foreign exchange interbank market due to speculative selling, traders said.
The rate was down from Monday's 8.2978.
The yuan opened slightly higher at 8.2975. After hitting an intra-day high of 8.2973 early in the session, it slipped to move mostly around the 8.2980 level before closing at a low.
Trading was dull, with most done at 8.2980, traders said.
Dealers said that, although speculative selling depressed the yuan's uptrend today, its downside space was limited.
"As the yuan has fallen in the past two days, a few sell offers emerged at about 8.2970 which hurt the strong pro-yuan sentiment," said one dealer.
But he said that the yuan would not lose much because there were good bids just above the key 8.3000 level.
A second dealer said central bank intervention and follow-up yuan-selling would be the only factors driving down the rates in the face of active buying expected in the short term.
"The central bank is likely to take action in the market in the short term if the price moves too sharply," he said.
Dealers expect the yuan to move around 8.2980 tomorrow.
The yuan closed slightly down at 7.2490 from 7.2420 against 100 Japanese yen and unchanged at 1.0715 against the Hong Kong dollar.
